reconstructed_theorem_text: Let (Omega,m,mu) be a finite measure space with filtration F on nonnegative time; T>0; and B a scalar Brownian motion with F satisfying the usual conditions. Here scalar Brownian motion with filtration means centered Gaussian finite-dimensional laws with covariance min(s,t), mu-almost surely continuous paths, strong F-adaptedness, and independence of B(t)-B(s) from F_s for every s<=t. Zero at time zero is part of the scalar law almost surely. Usual conditions mean that every mu-null subset of Omega is in every F_t, and F is right-continuous. Let q be a dyadic elementary process on [0,T]. It has a level l in N, N=2^l, times t_i=i*T/N for i=0,...,N (strictly increasing), and coefficients c_i:Omega->R, each strongly F_{t_i}-measurable and pointwise bounded: for every i there exists C_i in R such that |c_i(omega)|<=C_i for every omega. Its value is q(t,omega)=sum_{i=0}^{N-1} 1_{t_i<t<=t_{i+1}} c_i(omega). Embed this exact value process into the progressive L2 integrands on [0,T]. A progressive L2 integrand is a real process strongly progressive for F and in L2(mu product lambda_T), where lambda_T is Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T], transported to NNReal. I_eta denotes its specified continuous completed Ito integral against the given scalar Brownian driver: the canonical limit of elementary integrals, set to zero on its exceptional null set, and held constant after T. For every i=0,...,N-1, I_q(t_{i+1},omega)-I_q(t_i,omega)=c_i(omega)*(B(t_{i+1},omega)-B(t_i,omega)) for mu-almost every omega.
objects: Finite measure space, filtration F, positive horizon T, scalar B, dyadic elementary q with level l, grid t_i and bounded adapted coefficients, cell index i, Ito process I_q.
domains: NNReal time; real Brownian/process/coefficient values; i in Fin(2^q.level); mu finite.
quantifiers: For every space,F,mu,T,B,q and valid Brownian/usual hypotheses, and for every chosen grid-cell index i, the equality holds mu-a.e.
assumptions: T>0; scalar Brownian with F; F usual; q has fixed dyadic strictly increasing grid, left-endpoint strongly measurable coefficients, and per-coefficient pointwise bounds.
conclusion: Increment of completed Ito integral across a cell equals that cell coefficient times the Brownian increment, mu-a.e.
scopes: Equality at the two endpoints of the selected cell; statement quantifies i outside the a.e. equality. Coefficient formula uses open-left/closed-right cells. No equality for every omega is claimed.
constant_dependencies: Level,grid,coefficients are q data. Each C_i can depend on q and i but is uniform in omega. The integral uses B,mu,F,T and q.
